item.title: Printer that does not run out of ink or paper
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

Genre (Optional): Comedy

Elevator Pitch: It's just a printer that does not run out of ink or paper

Central Narrative: None

Hook/Attention-Grabber: If a certain quota of pages are not printed every 24hrs, then the printer will proceed to print out random images from the internet, at 5px/mm2, regardless if weather the image should be printable on the printer itself at that scale, i.e. the paper scales to match the size of the image. This process will carry on for 24 hrs with no known way to stop it, and will occur regardless if the device is power or not

item.title: Re: Requesting greenlight for SCP (Tune in Next Time)
item.content:encoded:
You had my interest but then the Hook/Attention-Grabber sorta lost me. Mysterious radio signal from a defunct radio tower and all it does is announce when someone is going to get attacked by a murder monster? I'm sorry, I feel like this idea could work better with something else at its core.

Also… connecting something that's been around since the 1600s with a radio tower is a strange choice, as that technology didn't exist until the 1920s or 30s. Its tonally discordant.

Moreover, there was no web addresses when the station became abandoned (you said between 1985-1990)… additionally it is unclear when the signal first started.

Finally, I think you need to think about what the narrative is. Because what you have here is a premise, without really telling us what the arc of the article will be. So its discovered, and….. is this just going to be a catalogue of murder monster events? Unless you have a story under the surface of these events you haven't mentioned, I think its too thin.

I think you should take this back to the drawing board… instead of this thing randomly, or selectively, choosing a victim for some monster I think it could be more interesting with a subtler anomaly.

item.title: Re: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
The idea came to me watching a hypercube building block demonstration. […] I imagined how a 4+ dimensional entity would appear to us […] This inter-dimensional nature of the beast is the whole point.

I don't see any of that reflected in the current concept presented. If you want to focus on the wonders of thinking in more than 3 dimensions, don't have the core anomaly focused on the terrible things it does.

+ show block
– hide block

As I understand it D-Class are recruited from death row inmates. Someone convicted of a sadistic murder should be at the top of their list. Additionally, from my reading, D-Class are directly exposed to anomalies all the time

The issue here is that you're assuming that the in-universe Foundation would conveniently happen to recruit this anomaly as a D-Class, and conveniently test it enough to expose it to multiple anomalies. As a reader, I find the entire setup questionable, since not only is it odd that the Foundation thought that this "sadistic murderer" person was someone they could just lump in with all the other D-Class, they also trusted them enough to expose them to multiple anomalies, rather than one or two. Granted, some readers may suspend their disbelief enough to not be too bothered by this setup, but combined with all the other plot contrivances the storyline for me seems more authorial meddling than believably developing narrative.

It's triggered on purpose by the Anomalous-D while being tasked with routine maintenance. An example might be purposefully breaking eye-contact with SCP-173 while cleaning its cell in order to feed off the trauma of either the creature or the other D-Class in the room

Again, if the dude is a sadistic murderer with no sense of self-preservation or empathy, why is the Foundation trusting them with anything? If they really want to use the guy as a lab rat, it would be for protocols with the absolute simplest instructions and plenty of safeguards in case the guy goes rogue. For this case I personally feel like an in-universe researcher would deem the guy not worth the trouble to test on (unless the nature of the anomaly necessitates a test subject who is almost ludicrously volatile and dangerous).

But they have. The SCP-682-E addendum recounts exactly this. And it makes perfect sense. There are at least two entities that I can think of that are on a termination list and the Foundation doesn't know how they're going to kill them.

SCP-682 was written almost a decade ago and is one dangerous anomaly out of thousands. Most readers aren't going to take your premise seriously if you need to rely on super-old (and frankly, not great examples of current site standards) Series I articles to support your reasoning for the Foundation acting irrationally.

I'm also playing with the notion that our thoughts, souls and emotions do exist on planes that we don't have conscious access to. Yet our emotions and souls are tied to our bodies, and in that way we are all extra-dimensional beings.

You might want to consider a tale or GoI format entry then, since the level of non-observable knowledge required to understand this thing empirically seems to necessitate omnipresence that the in-universe Foundation wouldn't have.

I've highlighted its potential because I'm thinking of the stories that follow next. If this entity is to live in isolation it will be just like so many others. It will be just another mystery in a box that says nothing about the larger world and how things work together. To me that is uninteresting.

If the core article is downvoted to deletion range, it doesn't matter how many stories beyond the first page you've planned. Focus on making the SCP entity enjoyable to read as a standalone first, and then if the audience response to it is good then you can start think about branching out. If you try too hard to force openings for additional followup works, it'll just feel contrived and overreaching.

In general though, I feel like your plans for the page are way more complicated and large-scale than I personally would enjoy reading about. At this point I think your best bet is to reach out to authors of high-rated extradimensional SCP articles (you can find them with the Tag Search) and see what they think of what you have planned.

item.title: Re: Weird Question
item.content:encoded:
Personally I feel like D-Class that are fleshed out as characters with backgrounds, unique or ongoing skills, and personalities often improve SCPs, especially if there's a lot of interaction with them in logs. Also especially if they survive through multiple SCPs. SCP-2515 and SCP-4479 are great examples. D-11424 even has their own tag.

I mean, from a document "realism" standpoint, they wouldn't mention background unless it was relevant to the testing (like in 2515), but 1) "realism" is highly overrated and 2) it can still come up in natural conversation.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: The Architects Automaton
item.content:encoded:
It is not yet known what happens when SCP-XXXX is allowed to finish one of its patterns, but it is certainly best left to conjecture.

Why? No need to be vague when trying to sell your idea

This is by no means something that could be elevator pitched, to say the least, and yes it will be incredibly difficult to achieve.

And yet, this is what is required for greenlighting. I would suggest you streamline the idea and give us the overall points/plot and themes you're going for.

  • Instead of listing out possible other things connected to this skip, focus on selling us why we would want to read about it. What are the stakes? What is the narrative? Even cosmic horror is dependent on an arc. Yes you can be vague and hinty in the article, but here you're meant to sell the idea.
  • things that make you go crazy are a) boring, because it was done to death, and b) sorta demeaning to those who have atypical neuro states. But a) is the real problem for a story… I would suggest thinking of some other effect seeing the patterns does… The unbearable information driving someone crazy has been old news since the 1920s. Stretch your imagination, this automaton could make designs that could do anything… why make people crazy? What else could be done to make it unsettling?

I suggest you take a good look at your ultimate point, and spell it out clearly in the idea post. You can edit it by clicking on options in the post and then edit.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Seeking Greenlight: The Architects Automaton

Absolutely delightful. I love the nonchalantness of the old woman. Like, she puts in a little effort to hide her "trophy husbands" but freely allows the officer to discover them with only the slightest pressure. There's not even any indication that she resists arrest. It almost feels like this behavior is one of those cultural or knowledge "blind spots" people have. Sure she has a vague enough sense that she doesn't want authorities to see her collection, but at the same time she's pretty sure this is what people mean when they talk about a "trophy spouse" and she's been doing it for long enough that the sunk cost fallacy comes into play.

Also the detail that the heads respire, and are alive on (im assuming) a cellular level is intriguing. I imagine they have base reflexes like following things with their eyes, and blinking in sunlight as well. The fact that they respite makes me wonder if they would sneeze if iritated. The even more deep questions arise about their level of mental activity. Is it possible they have something akin to shut-in syndrome? Just a trove of interesting things to consider

unfortunately i can only give it +1, but it is a +1 more than earned

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
The narrative of the article is the story of that MTF and their gradual transformation from hopeful, to weary to despairing and begging for rescue. At first they help the foundation in any way they can by communicating with them an informing them of the anomaly and trying to help them document it. Their lack of senses hinder this but they are able to logically deduce where they are and are able to 'sense' the other intangible objects around and in them. After a while they realize they won't be rescued and fall into despair, slowly suffocating as they become tangible enough to need to breath.

As for the communications issue, this is a Foundation long-distance communicator utilizing anomalous tech. As for not being able to see it, at least one of the MTF member down there is able to touch-type from muscle memory.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: “Patient Zero”
item.content:encoded:
Hey there eNCiVi, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither an official reviewer (but I am a flight officer) nor a hugely experienced one, so take everything I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let's begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
- Close Section-by-Section -

Elevator Pitch

So my main problem with this pitch is in two parts: it is quite overpowered (OP) and it is a humanoid (not a problem in itself, but I'll explain further along).
OP anomalies break the suspension of disbelief of readers if not executed correctly, and said execution is hard to do. Without this execution, OP anomalies feel slightly ridiculous and unrealistic, a surefire way to get downvotes on your article.
Humanoids are one of the hardest types of anomaly to write. Similarly to OP anomalies, they require great execution to not become downvote magnets. Without proper execution, they don't fit with the tone of the Site and feel more like a comic-book character rather than an SCP.

Central Narrative

There isn't very much here in regards to narrative. All you have is some testing logs and a vague incident which you fail to elaborate on because it is TBD1. This may have been acceptable in Series I, but people expect more in Series VI. Find an emotion you want the readers to feel, and use it to build up your narrative.

Hook/Attention Grabber

This is frustratingly vague and nothing more. Don't keep up the 'mystery' of your concept and try to keep it secret after posting in the forums, explain it! Tell us what the mystery is and what's behind it, otherwise it just makes it harder to critique your idea.

+ Open General Thoughts +
I'm quite doubtful about this

To put it bluntly, your anomaly is an OP humanoid which has little to no story behind it besides a vague 'incident' which isn't elaborated on. Not only this, but it is strange to me that it is only immune to the abilities of some of the most dangerous SCPs. Why? I am also getting slight self-insert 'vibes' (for lack of a better word that comes to mind) from this concept, which isn't good. I'd recommend it four things:

1. Consider reworking your concept. As it stands, it's quite OP and contrived.
2. Rework your narrative. Elaborate! Make me feel something!
3. Check out the Guide Hub for advice and essays on how to do the above two points. It's a great resource!
4. Contact some reviewers from the Butterfly Squad, they have tonnes of experience and are able to provide some great crit!


Anyway, that's it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!
Footnotes
1. Always finish off your idea before posting it in the forums, otherwise it makes it more difficult for us critters to critique it.

item.title: The Empathy Infection
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama

Page Layout: Standard containment procedures, description, discovery, testing logs and containment report.

Elevator Pitch: A sculpture of "The Three Graces" that spreads an memetic infection of emotional empathy. It was commissioned from an anartist for the Manna Charitable Foundation as an attempt to increase charitable acts. In particular, acts that include helping people normally considered of a lower class or importance. This extends to trying to protect these individuals from harm.

Any close viewing of charitable acts caused by the infection further spreads it to the viewer. The effect can also be spread through images and videos. This allows online spread of the memetic effect though literal viral posts and stories.

Central Narrative: Sites near [liberal city] experiences difficulty treating D-class as disposable and accepting collateral loss of life. An investigation looks into the situation and also finds increased charity efforts and the near elimination of homelessness in a large portion of the country. Further investigation discovers the infection. Originating from the sculpture newly installed in the city's downtown area.

The foundation confiscates the statue and tests antimemes for internal use. The site regains the ability to find D-Class suffering and death acceptable via the antimemetics. Using online bots they deploy these antimemes within disparaging and skeptical comments on the viral posts. Nearly all posts are effected and debased as either attention seeking or faked. This extents into offline instances being 'inoculated' by onlookers heckling and mocking the charitable acts.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Exploring the idea that the foundation works beyond compassion. Thus cannot exist in a world that is dedicated to it.

Additional Notes: I'm playing with the idea that the foundation is worried the viral posts could become resistant. Thus they are forced to worry not if they are too immoral, but too moral in their acts.

item.title: Re: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for this review. You've put a lot of work into it and I appreciate that. Having said that, I am left wondering if the content is actually this bad or if i've just failed to convey what I'm trying to do.

The idea came to me watching a hypercube building block demonstration. You can see it here.

I imagined how a 4+ dimensional entity would appear to us if some part of it were to intersect with our 3 D reality. I think we would perceive it as an anomaly.

In the story I'm trying to construct, a creature like SCP 682 is potentially vast – existing simultaneously across multiple dimensions. SCP researchers are vainly trying to terminate the thing by finding novel ways to blast the small fraction of it that they’ve snared in our reality.

I'm inspired to work along these lines because I'm interested in root causes. The SCP universe is now populated by something like 5000 anomalies with little sense of coherent rhyme. I'm excited by the opportunity to contribute to cannon in a way that suggests an inter-relationship between phenomena. Make some of them make a little more sense.

+ show block
– hide block

don't make this thing an interdimensional traveler.

This inter-dimensional nature of the beast is the whole point. Its existence across dimensions is what gives me the opportunity to play with interconnection between anomalies along planes that we humans don't have access to.

don't have the Foundation recruit it as a D-Class.

As I understand it D-Class are recruited from death row inmates. A drifter with no family who's been convicted of a sadistic murder should be at the top of their list. Additionally, from my reading, D-Class are directly exposed to anomalies all the time

don't have there be a random breach that randomly involves the entity.

The breach would not be random. It's triggered on purpose by the Anomalous-D while being tasked with routine maintenance. An example might be purposefully breaking eye-contact with SCP-173 while cleaning its cell in order to feed off the trauma of either the creature or the other D-Class in the room

the Foundation has contained tons of dangerous anomalies that could injure or destroy other anomalies, but they're not clamoring to use those either

But they have. The SCP-682-E addendum recounts exactly this. And it makes perfect sense. There are at least two entities that I can think of that are on a termination list and the Foundation doesn't know how they're going to kill them.

give it more emotional/intellectual depth than "does terrible things, makes people feel bad, because that's what it was conceptualized to do". Does it have any self-awareness of what has to do to survive? Does it have any redeeming qualities as an individual? This would be the main spot to flesh out, since generic danger effects are pretty common, and often seen in low-rated and deleted works.

Admittedly my thoughts here are less complete. But what I'm working with is the idea that it's a chameleon which takes on the shapes of the reality that it inhabits. It has no emotions and it's not truly sapient. It functions like an extremely sophisticated chatbot mimicking the patterns around it (I am aware of the problems of squaring that with its passing as a D-Class human for weeks).

It stays in one reality only as long as it can feed and then it drifts into another.

I'm also playing with the notion that our thoughts, souls and emotions do exist on planes that we don't have conscious access to. Yet our emotions and souls are tied to our bodies, and in that way we are all extra-dimensional beings. Anomalous-D feeds on the part of us (of all things) that's not corporal. It is able to heighten our emotional states by torturing our corporal bodies. Like squeezing juice from a fruit.

remove the unusually insistent focus on this thing's "potential" usefulness.

I've highlighted its potential because I'm thinking of the stories that follow next. If this entity is to live in isolation it will be just like so many others. It will be just another mystery in a box that says nothing about the larger world and how things work together. To me that is uninteresting.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: SCP Idea SEEKING GREENLIGHT
item.content:encoded:
Page type: New SCP Article
Elevator Pitch: This SCP would be something simple, something that makes you wonder "How can a Hot-air balloon do this?"
Central Narrative: ISo my SCP is a man in a hot air balloon that is designated safe as he only attacks in self defense. The Hot-Air balloon itself can reach up to extremely fast speeds and stop on a time and do things such as move in any direction or things like barrel rolls. A real physics breaking type entity. For example, the Balloon can easily reach Mach 3 and then stop instantly with no inertia, no drag, nothing and the man in said balloon doesn't fly out of the balloon or do any type of bracing for the oncoming stop. The SCP itself can initiate maneuvers such as barrel rolls.
Hook: The hook is that it has that funny/weird feel to it while not being that ridiculous that it takes people of out it.
From what I read I have to get the concept greenlight then the draft and then the final green light for it to become and "Canon" article.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for SCP
item.content:encoded:
So there's already a few magical archives/libraries on the wiki… Obviously the Wanderer's Library and also Alexandria Eternal…

What about your story would set it apart from these very well understood concepts?

Additionally:

One agent emerges from the skip physically unharmed, but showing symptoms of psychological trauma. The agent can't remember what may have caused said trauma or why they are the only member of their task force on record. The Foundation can tell something is up and suspends testing. This is not the first time this sequence has repeated, perhaps end the article with the start of a new cycle of testing and forgetting.

This doesn't really explain what's going on. It's all good to be mysterious in the article but if you want evaluation on the idea, you'll have to be more transparent… So, what is in the archive?

Finally, this is missing much in the way of a narrative. What arc is there to your article? Where do we start vs. where do we end? What's the plot? Are there themes? Are there characters?

item.title: Re: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. I'll be honest, this kind of seems like SCP-1655 (Sorrow Tick), but overpowered to an extreme degree.

+ show block
– hide block

I am admittedly skeptical of nearly everything in the initial setup:

  • remember the difference between sentient and sapient. Plenty of animals are considered sentient—if you want human-level intelligence and self-awareness, use "sapient".
  • it seems odd that this extradimensional entity just happened to both be capable of taking a human form and also blending in with human society well enough so as to not be immediately noticed as not human.
  • it also feels like a stretch that the individual just happened to have been picked up by the Foundation as a D-Class.
  • it also feels like a stretch that the Foundation would have just let this thing in "frequent close proximity of various other anomalies", especially given that the individual was seemingly convicted for tons of crimes which would make it unreliable at best, completely useless at worst, as a test subject who would be expected to take instruction as part of experimental protocol.

The rest of the story just seems like a mishmash of various commonly seen cliché story beats that don't really genuinely increase tension so much as artificially force more danger into the narrative simply to increase drama. You've got the spontaneous unexplained security breach (granted, if the reader headcanons the Foundation as not being hyper-competent like I do, there's more wiggle room here for sudden mistakes), the "sole survivor" main character, the obligatory death of a staff member, the "is it more important/terrible/powerful than we originally thought??" pondering, and the completely unnecessary consideration of using this poorly understood, uncontrollable anomaly for Foundation purposes (I saw in the original post that there was a thought of reclassifying the anomaly as Keter or Thaumiel—I recommend that you don't do that. The thing isn't Keter if it's not a big deal if no one's close enough for it to mess with, and there's no way the Foundation would ever consider it Thaumiel because it's too unpredictable and untrustworthy to ever be a reliable form of containment. Being potentially useful for keeping something locked up is not the same as being the active containment that keeps something locked up).

Personally I would recommend that you shelve this concept for now, and return to it after you have the experience of a successful article or two written. This is a pretty difficult premise to work with because of how inherently overpowered and unlikable the main entity is (it literally exists to make other people feel bad—the average reader isn't likely to be emotionally attached to that sort of entity) and how you're intending to portray the Foundation as attributing a lot more significance to the anomaly than makes sense from an objective perspective. Remember, you as the author inherently ascribe value to the entity, but the in-universe Foundation has no obligation to try and grasp at straws to find a use for this thing. Statements like this:

the possibility that this new anomaly may be used to injure or possibly destroy other anomalies is cannot be ignored.

are admittedly difficult for readers to take seriously, since the Foundation has contained tons of dangerous anomalies that could injure or destroy other anomalies, but they're not clamoring to use those either.

If you really want to try writing this, I feel like you would need to at least do the following:

  • don't make this thing an interdimensional traveler. You can have it be alien-ish in origin, but it should have a solid familiarity with Earth/people if it's going to prey on people specifically.
  • give it more emotional/intellectual depth than "does terrible things, makes people feel bad, because that's what it was conceptualized to do". Does it have any self-awareness of what has to do to survive? Does it have any redeeming qualities as an individual? This would be the main spot to flesh out, since generic danger effects are pretty common, and often seen in low-rated and deleted works. SCPs don't need to be dangerous to be successful.
  • don't have the Foundation recruit it as a D-Class.
  • don't have there be a random breach that randomly involves the entity.
  • remove the unusually insistent focus on this thing's "potential" usefulness.

item.title: New SCP: Book of irreligious obsession
item.content:encoded:
A book titled “The Figments of the Mind” by Mark Desoreau causes religious readers to abandon their faith, and and redirect that energy towards a harmless hobby, growing obnoxious and violent as they obsess with it.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Howdy folks, new here, though I remember when 173 was just an /x/ post. I've always wanted to write an SCP but never had any good ideas, until one struck me a couple weeks ago. It's ready to post, but I'm here for Greenlight first - I hope I'm following all the correct protocols!

As the summary says, it's a seemingly innocuous text - the first instance discovered was titled “The Figments of the Mind” by Mark Desoreau - which appears to be a fairly basic work of the pro-reason/anti-superstition genre - but when read by anyone of deep religious convictions, it causes them to gradually abandon their religion, and then take up a new hobby to replace it. UFOs, online gaming, RPG universes - first they abandon work and alienate their friends and family, then (in 70% of suspected cases in the wild) they eventually become violent.

Futhermore, it appears that this text keeps cropping up throughout history, with an Ur copy in the 15th century, although a possible precursor is mentioned by Tacitus in describing Nero.

The whole thing is a meta-critique on how people can go crazy forming cults out of the weirdest things, and while they might not seem dangerous at first, at the minimum it can lead to disastrous life outcomes, dragging their friends and family down.

I've done what I can to embed it in the universe (the first Alpha instance was a guy obsessed with SCP-1425 Star Signals, but who'd never read that book - it turns out that was just his 'hobby obsession'). I definitely wouldn't mind some critiques from the more detail-oriented people in improving my cross-SCP references.

I hope you like the idea - tell me if/when you want it in Sandbox.

item.title: Re: The Macguffin
item.content:encoded:
MAJOR CHANGES

Well then, I know it’s been a while but I think I know what to do.

Earlier I said that the Foundation couldn’t aim this artifact. I’m changing that, they did weaponize it, for a time. The main thing I’m changing is the way it targets a villain. Instead of the locket having its own sense of right and wrong it targets someone the holder views as evil. The thing is, it targets anyone nearby that is evil enough, that’s always been how it works I’m just making it clear.

What I’m planning on adding is a program where the Foundation uses the locket to defeat some small GOIs. It works, for a time. Then during one attempt, the holder of the locket turns around and proceeds to attack the Foundation. Causing serious damage and even unseating a site administrator. After being interviewed the holder confesses that they’d been questioning the morality of the Foundation for some time but had never thought of doing anything about it. That’s when the Foundation realizes that no amount of psychology or loyalty tests can tell if someone truly, in their heart of hearts, believes the Foundation is good. So they discontinue the program.

item.title: Re: -1
item.content:encoded:
Offering my two cents as the author, I believe you unfortunately misread the whole article.

So, the first point. It's not anomalous, you say. For context, this article takes place in 2022, two years after the bushfires have occurred. Safe to say, if thousands of koalas1 still disappear at that point, without any fires, that would be utterly anomalous, right? I mean, it's the symbol of Australia, and someone's bound to notice the fact that they're disappearing.

Plus, I don't think large, flying serpents are a species native to Australia, because if that's the case, then I would be saving up in order to ride on those. Second, koalas are cute, and I won't trade those for snakes.

Second, I'm not sure on your thoughts about the pacing. You say "greatly written" at the start but then dismiss my article's pacing and narrative as a joke.

Choose one - it's ok if you found the article unsatisfying, but I'm just really confused about what you said.

Additionally, all people I asked did not point out that my article was too sparse and unnaturally progressing, and I'm against the idea that environmental action against climate change is a joke, so I have my doubts on everything you said.

Lastly, the ending (Incident DROPBEAR) was crafted in order to suit the New Year. Look, I don't want to shoehorn drama, politics2 and angst into this whole thing just to reduce the possible "that's it?"moment, because that would detract from the whole koala and aboriginal culture angle.

Plus, I'm simply basing off the fact that Dreamtime is rooted in the concept of an everywhen - the fact that it is timeless, so I actually don't feel good about you saying that this is a joke.

Footnotes
1. You should also note that even those in zoos - safe from bushfires - disappeared.
2. Australian politics are a whole another level, and as a Filipino, I didn't dare touch on that deeply.
